citation.title: Intrinsic Fluctuation and Its Critical Scaling in a Class of Populations of Oscillators with Distributed Frequencies

how_reached: Full five-page scan read page by page via the OUP article-pdf route.
why_this_source: This is where the asymmetry actually first appears — the paper the catalogue should have been citing, and the only primary Daido text in this pass that carries both sides of the pair.
observable: FLUCTUATION. sigma = lim sqrt(N) <|Z - <Z>|^2>^(1/2) under a long time average. Note the square root: Daido's exponents are on sigma, the modern literature's are on chi = sigma^2.
frequency_class: REGULAR / deterministic-quantile, Lorentzian half-width gamma = 1e-3, random initial conditions only.

quotes.locator: p. 727, text preceding and including Eq. (2)
quotes.quote: On the other hand, for finite-size systems, it was found numerically that Z exhibits persistent fluctuation whose magnitude σ, defined by σ=lim_{N→∞}√N⟨|Z−⟨Z⟩|²⟩^{1/2}, behaves as   σ(ε)∝|ε−ε_c|^{−γ′}   (2)   near the threshold ε_c.
quotes.bears_on: THE OBSERVABLE, in Daido's own words: a dynamic fluctuation of the order parameter, and defined on sqrt(N*Var), not on N*Var.

quotes.quote: σ(ε)≅f̃(0)√(ε_c/|b|)(ε_c−ε)^{−1/2} ,   (12)   where b=(2/π²)∫₀^∞ dy f̃′(y)/y with f̃′≡df̃/dy. Therefore γ′=1/2 for ε<ε_c.
quotes.bears_on: SUBCRITICAL: gamma' = 1/2 on sigma, exact. Squared into chi units this is the modern gamma' = 1.

quotes.quote: σ(ε)∝(ε−ε_c)^{−1/8}   (17)   near ε_c. Namely, γ′=1/8 for ε>ε_c.
quotes.bears_on: SUPERCRITICAL: gamma' = 1/8 on sigma. Squared into chi units this is the modern gamma = 1/4. Note Daido labels BOTH sides gamma'.

quotes.quote: Remarkably the critical exponent γ′ is not the same for below and above ε_c. When compared to previous numerical results,⁵⁾ the theory is consistent with γ′=0.123±0.003 for ε>ε_c while it disagrees with γ′=0.126±0.009 for ε<ε_c.
quotes.bears_on: Daido's OWN numerics were symmetric at ~1/8 on sigma (~1/4 on chi), statistically indistinguishable from what Hong et al. later measure. The asymmetry is his perturbation theory disagreeing with his own data.

quotes.quote: The reason for the discrepancy of the result in Ref. 5) with the theory in the subcritical regime is now clear: As is evident in Fig. 1(a), the finite-size effect is so strong there that N=1600 chosen in Ref. 5) was still too small.
quotes.bears_on: Daido's stated reason for preferring the subcritical theory over his own measurement. This is exactly the claim Hong et al. later overturn at larger N.

quotes.quote: A finite-size scaling analysis has been performed with N larger than in Ref. 5) to get conclusive evidence for σ which is expected to fit   σ=N^{1/4}Ψ(|ε−ε_c|N^s) ,   (18)   where s=2, Ψ(x)∼x^{−1/8}(x≫1) for ε>ε_c (as first proposed and verified in Ref. 5)), and s=1/2, Ψ(x)∼x^{−1/2}(x≫1) for ε<ε_c.
quotes.bears_on: Daido's FSS ansatz, and the origin of the nu-bar ~ 1/2 and nu-bar' ~ 2 that Hong et al. reject.

quotes.quote: Evidence is presented in Fig. 1 which was obtained for f̃(Δ)=(γ/π)(Δ²+γ²)^{−1} with γ=10^{−3}, and for fairly random initial conditions.
quotes.bears_on: Distribution axis: Lorentzian, and a reminder that gamma here is the half-width.

quotes.quote: *) While numerical simulations in Refs. 4) and 5) are for a discrete-time model, their results may be viewed as virtually for the model (1) owing to the small width of f(Ω) adopted.
quotes.bears_on: Model-class caveat: Daido's numerical evidence is a discrete-time circle-map system, transferred to the ODE by an argument, not by measurement.

quotes.quote: 4) H. Daido, Prog. Theor. Phys. 75 (1986), 1460.   5) H. Daido, J. of Phys. A20 (1987), L629.   6) H. Daido, preprint (July 1988).
quotes.bears_on: Daido cites PTP 75, 1460 (1986) as the numerical antecedent, not as the source of the asymmetric exponents.

numbers: FLUCTUATION | regular Lorentzian | SUBcritical | Eq. (12): gamma' = 1/2 on sigma, exact (analytic, no error bar). ==> 1 on chi.
FLUCTUATION | regular Lorentzian | SUPERcritical | Eq. (17): gamma' = 1/8 on sigma, approximate. ==> 1/4 on chi.
FLUCTUATION | regular Lorentzian | Daido's own numerics (from J. Phys. A 20, L629 (1987)): 0.123 +/- 0.003 above, 0.126 +/- 0.009 below, on sigma. ==> 0.246(6) and 0.252(18) on chi — symmetric.
FSS | Eq. (18): sigma = N^(1/4) Psi(|eps - eps_c| N^s), s = 2 above, s = 1/2 below.
caveats: A Note added in proof flags an inconsistency in the A_+ approximation but states 'The result (17), however, remains unchanged'.
Daido uses the single symbol gamma' for the exponent on BOTH sides; the modern gamma/gamma' split is a later relabelling.
